findings.description: Universal Claude Code permission rules are not matched. `Bash(*)` becomes the exact key `=*`, while bare `Bash` is discarded. Neither can match any required command.
findings.failure_mode: A configuration granting all Bash commands reports required permissions as missing. Conversely, a universal Bash deny combined with command-specific allows is ignored, so the checker reports permissions as available even though the harness denies every command.
findings.suggested_fix: Normalize both universal forms to a dedicated key and consult that key for every requirement, applying universal denies before any allows. Add coverage for both universal allow and universal deny rules.

findings.description: The opt-in `implement_gate.mode: authoritative` path now trusts `tool_input.active_skill`, which the header comment itself states is model-authored. Previously authoritative mode was selected only when detect-platform-features.sh had observed a harness-set field; now the operator flips it on with no harness attestation, so once enabled the model can self-declare `active_skill: implement` on any App-Zone Write/Edit and the gate waves it through. The evidence recorder is correctly inert (it never changes the mode, merges via `$b + {...}`, writes atomically, and is gated on lead session / no agent_id), so no state clobber there; but writing `active_skill_available: false` unconditionally will overwrite a `true` that detect-platform-features.sh may have recorded in the same key.
findings.failure_mode: An operator who sets the undocumented opt-in gets a gate that is weaker than heuristic mode: any App-Zone write with a model-supplied `active_skill` string bypasses the fail-ask. Separately, the recorder can flip `active_skill_available` from true to false on the first qualifying payload.
findings.suggested_fix: In authoritative mode, require BOTH the payload `active_skill` AND the heuristic RUNNING state (AND, not OR), or at least log an audit.jsonl event when the authoritative path allows a write that heuristic mode would have asked about. Have the recorder write only `active_skill_seen_at` and `active_skill_source`, leaving `active_skill_available` to detect-platform-features.sh.

findings.description: Two regressions versus `base_pattern_of`. (1) `rule_key "$perm"` for a required rule is called without `|| ...`; `rule_key` returns 1 for anything not shaped `Bash(...)`, and the script runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so a single non-Bash entry in `all_required` (e.g. a future `WebFetch(domain:...)` or bare `Read`) aborts the preflight with a silent exit 1 instead of reporting it as missing. The old helper never failed. (2) For an exact required rule (`Bash(git push)` → key `=git push`), the base derivation `base="*${key#\*}"` does not strip the `=` sentinel, producing `*=git`, which can never match an allow or deny key. Previously `Bash(git:*)` covered an exact required `Bash(git push)`; now only an identical exact allow rule does.
findings.failure_mode: If any required rule is non-Bash the checker dies mid-loop with no report; if any required rule is exact-form, it is reported missing even when a covering `Bash(cmd:*)` wildcard is allowed, and a `Bash(cmd:*)` deny no longer blocks it.
findings.suggested_fix: `rule_key "$perm" || { missing_permissions+=("$perm"); continue; }` and derive base from the body regardless of sentinel: `body="${key#[*=]}"; base="*${body%% *}"`. Add a bats case with an exact required rule covered by a wildcard allow, and one with a non-Bash required rule.

findings.description: The claude-opus-5-5 entry omits `pricing.long_context` citing the vendor sentence that 4.6-and-later models include the full 1M window at standard pricing. That same sentence applies to the sibling opus-5, sonnet-5, fable-5-1 and fable-5 entries, which still carry a 2.0x/1.5x `long_context` tier (`verified: false`), and `test_five_family_declares_the_beta_header_list_and_the_long_context_tier` pins them to it while `test_entries_outside_the_five_family_carry_no_long_context_tier` pins 5.5 to the opposite. The catalog therefore encodes two contradictory readings of one vendor fact, and the tests lock the contradiction in. No runtime effect today because `effective_input_ceiling` (180K) sits under the 200K threshold, so the multiplier never fires through cheval.
findings.failure_mode: Cost reporting diverges by model for the same vendor pricing rule once any ceiling is probed above 200K; whichever reading is wrong will be silently wrong for a whole generation.
findings.suggested_fix: Pick one reading and apply it to all 4.6+ HTTP entries: either drop `long_context` from the FIVE_FAMILY set (and the tests that require it) with the same 2026-10-05 citation, or add it to 5.5 as `verified: false`. Record the decision in catalog-evidence.md.

findings.description: The defaults change from raw vendor model IDs (`gpt-4o`, `claude-3-opus-20240229`) to catalog aliases (`reviewer`, `opus`) under a block still titled 'API configuration'. Aliases resolve only through cheval/model-invoke. flatline-learning-extractor.sh carries an explicit cycle-103 note that it was migrated off direct `/v1/chat/completions`; this script carries no such note and its prior defaults were raw IDs, which is the signature of a direct-API caller. If any code path still POSTs `$GPT_MODEL` / `$OPUS_MODEL` to a vendor endpoint, `reviewer` and `opus` are invalid model names and every call 400s.
findings.failure_mode: Proposal review fails at runtime with a provider 'model not found' error on the default configuration, where it previously failed only on the retired-model error.
findings.suggested_fix: Confirm in the truncated body that every use of GPT_MODEL/OPUS_MODEL goes through model-invoke/cheval. If it does, add the cycle-103-style comment; if not, route it through cheval or keep concrete catalog IDs (`openai:gpt-5.5`, `anthropic:claude-opus-5-5`).

findings.description: Answering reviewer concern 1: binding a bare `:N` that is not glued to a path token to the last cited path is a grader defect, not acceptable noise. The LOA-VERDICT JSON trailer (`"critical":1`, `"high":0`, ...) is present in essentially every graded review, so every review that cites at least one path acquires a phantom `<last-path>:0` or `<last-path>:1` citation. A defect fixture at line 1 (file headers, shebangs, imports) is then 'recalled' spuriously, and cited-line totals are inflated uniformly, biasing the recall metric upward. The file is in the diff but truncated from this review, so the exact regex is unverified here.
findings.failure_mode: Recall scores are systematically inflated and defects on line 0/1 of any cited file are marked found regardless of review content.
findings.suggested_fix: Require the colon-number to be adjacent to a path-like token (no whitespace before the colon, preceded by `[A-Za-z0-9_./-]`), or strip the LOA-VERDICT trailer and other JSON before citation extraction. Add a fixture whose only `:N` is inside the verdict JSON and assert zero bound citations.

findings.cross_file_justification: The lengthened `why` strings in constraints.json regenerate into CLAUDE.loa.md, whose byte budget is checked by tools/check-prompt-budget.sh (in the diff, truncated); the budget was raised 9,216 → 10,240 and the generated file now sits at 10,225 bytes.
findings.description: This PR reverts the rationale diet (eleven `why` fields grow, e.g. the C-TEAM and spiraling rows), regenerates CLAUDE.loa.md, and raises the prompt budget to exactly absorb it, leaving 15 bytes of headroom. The next one-word edit to any constraint rationale, or any reference-table row, trips the budget check.
findings.failure_mode: CI fails on the next unrelated constraint text edit, and the likely remedy will be another budget bump with no principled ceiling.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the shorter rationales (the diet versions in tests/fixtures/constraint-rationales-pre-diet.json convey the same content) or set the budget with a stated margin (e.g. 10% over current) and document the rule in check-prompt-budget.sh.

findings.description: The diff's version of this test asserts `ceiling_calibration.source == 'conservative_default'` and `calibrated_at is None`, matching the catalog entry in the diff. The full-file head copy supplied for review is a different revision: it imports cycle-127 helpers (`_BETA_HEADER_RE`, `input_bound`, `is_foreign_transport_calibration`), asserts `'claude-opus-5-5' in foreign`, and in `test_lookup_returns_the_concrete_bound_through_the_gate_path` requires 5.5 to be calibrated with `effective_input_ceiling != 180000`. Against the catalog in this diff (calibrated_at: null, ceiling 180000) those head-copy tests fail. One of the two artefacts is stale relative to the other.
findings.failure_mode: If the supplied head copy is the true merge target, the test suite fails on merge; if the diff is the truth, the review context was built from the wrong revision and the generated-artefact consistency checks (checksum, maps) may also have been compared against the wrong base.
findings.suggested_fix: Re-run the Python suite on the actual merge base before approving; confirm which revision of test_anthropic_catalog_floor.py is head and that the catalog's 5.5 calibration state matches it.
